answer.short_answer: Ji haan, agar kisi muahiday (agreement) ka consideration ya maqsad (object) ghair qanooni (unlawful) ho, to woh muahida void hota hai.
answer.explanation: Qanoon ke mutabiq, har woh muahida jiska consideration ya object unlawful ho, woh void qarar diya jata hai.

citations.act_or_case: Lahore High Court | Writ Petition No.12069 of 2010
citations.quote: Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void.
A promises to obtain for B an employment in the public service, and B promises to pay 1,000 rupees to A. The agreement is void, as the consideration for it is unlawful.

answer.short_answer: Yes, you may demand the return of a gratuitously lent item at any time, but you may be liable to indemnify the borrower if the premature return causes them a loss that exceeds the benefit they derived from the loan.
answer.explanation: Under the Contract Act, 1872, a lender can require the return of a gratuitously lent item even before the agreed time or purpose is fulfilled. However, if the borrower has acted in reliance on the loan such that an early return causes them a loss greater than the benefit they received, the lender must indemnify the borrower for the excess loss.

citations.quote: The lender of a thing for use may at any time require its return, if the loan was gratuitous, even though he lent it for a specified time or purpose. But, if, on the faith of such loan made for a specified time or purpose, the borrower has acted in such a manner that the return of the thing lent before the time agreed upon would cause him loss exceeding the benefit actually derived by him from the loan, the lender must, if he compels the return, indemnify the borrower for the amount in which the loss so occasioned exceeds the benefit so derived.

answer.short_answer: Ji haan, agar koi muahida tora jaye jis ke natijay mein nuqsan ho, to nuqsan uthane wala fareeq muahida torne wale se harjana wasool karne ka haq rakhta hai.
answer.explanation: Qanoon-e-Muahida Act, 1872 ke mutabiq, jab koi muahida tora jata hai, to mutasira fareeq ko us nuqsan ya zarar ka muawza milne ka haq hai jo fitri tor par us muahiday ke tootne se waqay hua ho.

citations.quote: جب کوئی معاہدہ توڑ دیا گیا ہو، تو وہ فریق جو مذکور نقص معاہدہ کی وجہ سے نقصان اٹھائے، اس فریق سے جس نے معاہدہ توڑا ہو، اس نقصان یا ضرر کے لیے جو اس وجہ سے اسے ہوا ہو، معاوضہ وصول کرنے کا حق رکھتا ہے

answer.short_answer: جی ہاں، قانون معاہدہ ایکٹ کے تحت فریقِ متاثرہ معاہدہ توڑنے والے فریق سے اس نقصان یا ضرر کا معاوضہ وصول کرنے کا حق رکھتا ہے جو معاہدے کی خلاف ورزی کے نتیجے میں ہوا ہو، جس کا تخمینہ معاہدے میں طے شدہ رقم سے زیادہ بھی ہو سکتا ہے۔
answer.explanation: قانون معاہدہ ایکٹ، ۱۸۷۲ء کی دفعہ ۷۳ کے مطابق، جب کوئی معاہدہ توڑا جاتا ہے تو متاثرہ فریق اس نقصان یا ضرر کا معاوضہ وصول کرنے کا حقدار ہوتا ہے جو معاہدے کی خلاف ورزی کے نتیجے میں فطری طور پر وقوع پذیر ہوا ہو۔ قانون اس بات کی وضاحت کرتا ہے کہ معاوضے کا تخمینہ لگاتے وقت معاہدے کی عدم تکمیل کے باعث ہونے والی تکلیف کو دور کرنے کی کوششوں کا لحاظ رکھا جانا چاہیے۔

citations.quote: جب کوئی معاہدہ توڑ دیا گیا ہو، تو وہ فریق جو مذکورہ معاہدہ کی وجہ سے نقصان اٹھائے، اس فریق سے جس نے معاہدہ توڑا ہو، نقصان یا ضرر کے لیے جو اس وجہ سے اسے ہوا ہو، معاوضہ وصول کرنے کا حق رکھتا ہے

answer.short_answer: No, you are not entitled to hold the person liable for non-performance if the work cannot be executed due to your failure to provide the necessary materials or access.
answer.explanation: According to the Contract Act, 1872, if a party is required to supply necessary items for the execution of a contract and fails to do so, the other party is not required to perform the work and is not liable for non-performance; rather, the party who failed to provide the necessary items is liable to make compensation.

citations.quote: B supplying the scaffolding and timber necessary for the work. B refuses to furnish any scaffolding or timber, and he work cannot be executed. A need not execute the work, and B is bound to make compensation to A for any loss caused to him by the non-performance of the contract.

answer.short_answer: عوامی راستے پر لاپرواہی سے گاڑی چلانے کی صورت میں قید کی سزا ہو سکتی ہے۔
answer.explanation: مجموعہ تعزیرات پاکستان کے مطابق، اگر کوئی شخص عوامی راستے پر اس قدر لاپرواہی یا غفلت سے گاڑی چلائے جس سے انسانی زندگی کو خطرہ ہو یا کسی دوسرے شخص کو نقصان پہنچنے کا اندیشہ ہو، تو اسے قید کی سزا دی جا سکتی ہے۔

citations.quote: Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for

answer.short_answer: پاکستان پینل کوڈ کی دفعہ 357 کے تحت، کسی شخص کو غلط طریقے سے قید کرنے کی کوشش میں حملہ کرنے یا مجرمانہ طاقت استعمال کرنے والے شخص کو ایک سال تک قید، یا تین ہزار روپے تک جرمانہ، یا دونوں سزائیں دی جا سکتی ہیں۔
answer.explanation: پاکستان پینل کوڈ کی دفعہ 357 واضح کرتی ہے کہ جو کوئی بھی کسی شخص کو غلط طریقے سے قید کرنے کی کوشش میں اس پر حملہ کرے یا مجرمانہ طاقت کا استعمال کرے، وہ مذکورہ بالا سزا کا مستوجب ہوگا۔

citations.quote: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, in attempting wrongfully to confine that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to 3[three thousand rupees], or with both.

answer.short_answer: Under Section 123A of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, any person who advocates for the abolition of Pakistan's sovereignty or condemns the creation of the State in a manner prejudicial to its safety or ideology is subject to legal consequences.
answer.explanation: The law explicitly prohibits and criminalizes the act of condemning the creation of Pakistan or advocating for the abolition of its sovereignty, particularly when such actions are intended to influence the public in a way that is prejudicial to the safety or ideology of the State.

citations.quote: Whoever, within or without Pakistan, with intent to influence, or knowing it to be likely that he will influence, any person or the whole or any section of the public, in a manner likely to be prejudicial to the safety [or ideology] 15 of Pakistan, or to endanger the sovereignty of Pakistan in respect of all or any of the territories lying within its borders, shall by words, spoken or written, or by signs or visible representation,[abuse Pakistan or]15 condemn the creation of Pakistan by virtue of

answer.short_answer: Yes, an individual can be charged with cheating by personation even if the person they are pretending to be is imaginary.
answer.explanation: According to the Pakistan Penal Code, the offence of cheating by personation is committed regardless of whether the person being personated is a real or an imaginary individual.

citations.quote: The offence is committed whether the in dividual personated is a real or imaginary person.

answer.short_answer: Under Section 337Q of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, the arsh for the destruction (itlaf) of a single organ is equivalent to the value of diyat.
answer.explanation: The law specifies that for any organ found singly in the human body, such as the nose or tongue, the compensation payable as arsh is equal to the full value of diyat.

citations.quote: The arsh for causing itlaf of an organ which is found singly in a human body shall be equivalent to the value of diyat.

answer.short_answer: An intoxicated person who causes annoyance in a public place may be punished with simple imprisonment for up to twenty-four hours, a fine of up to thirty rupees, or both.
answer.explanation: Under Section 510 of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, appearing in a public place in a state of intoxication and conducting oneself in a manner that causes annoyance to others is a punishable offense.

citations.quote: Whoever, in a state of intoxication appears in any public place, or in any place which it is a trespass in him to enter, and there conducts himself in such a manner as to cause annoyance to any person, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to twenty-four hours, or with fine which may extend to 1[thirty] rupees, or with both.

answer.short_answer: The maximum term of imprisonment for causing mudihah to another person is five years.
answer.explanation: Under the Pakistan Penal Code, a person who causes mudihah is liable to daman and may also be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term extending up to five years as ta'zir.

citations.quote: (iv) mudihah to any person, shall be liable to daman and may also be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years as ta'zir

answer.short_answer: Yes, it is a criminal offense to accept gratification as a reward for using personal influence to induce a public servant to perform or forbear an official act.
answer.explanation: Under the Pakistan Penal Code, Section 163 explicitly criminalizes the act of accepting, obtaining, or attempting to obtain any gratification as a motive or reward for exercising personal influence over a public servant to perform or forbear an official act.

citations.quote: Whoever accepts or obtains, or agrees to accept or attempts to obtain, from any person, for himself or for any other person, any gratification whatever, as a motive or reward for in ducing, by the exercise of personal influence, any public servant to do or to forbear to do any official act... shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

answer.short_answer: Ji haan, National Assembly ke dissolve hone ki surat mein Federal Government kharchon ke liye funds authorize kar sakti hai.
answer.explanation: Aaeen ke mutabiq, jab National Assembly dissolve ho jaye to Federal Government kisi bhi maali saal mein chaar mah se zyada arsay ke liye Federal Consolidated Fund se ikhrajat authorize kar sakti hai.

citations.act_or_case: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
citations.quote: Notwithstanding anything contained in the foregoing provisions relating to financial matters, at any time when the National Assembly stands dissolved, the Federal Government may authorize expenditure from the Federal Consolidated Fund in respect of the estimated expenditure for a period not exceeding four months in any financial year

answer.short_answer: If a member of a Provincial Assembly is appointed as Governor, their seat in the Assembly becomes vacant on the day they enter upon their office.
answer.explanation: According to Article 103(2) of the Constitution, a Governor cannot be a member of a Provincial Assembly, and the appointment of such a member to the office of Governor results in the automatic vacation of their legislative seat upon assuming the new office.

citations.act_or_case: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
citations.quote: if a member of 1[Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament)] or a Provincial Assembly is appointed as Governor, his seat in 1[Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament)] or, as the case may be, the Provincial Assembly shall become vacant on the day he enters upon his office.

answer.short_answer: Federation ya Province ke liye appeal karne ki miyad faislay ke baad chhay (6) mahine hai.
answer.explanation: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973 ke Article 203F(1) ke tehat, Federation ya Province ko appeal karne ke liye chhay mahine ka waqt diya gaya hai.

citations.act_or_case: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
citations.quote: Provided that an appeal on behalf of the Federation or of a Province may be preferred within six months of such decision.

answer.short_answer: No, a court cannot validate an act of high treason.
answer.explanation: The Constitution explicitly prohibits any court, including the Federal Constitutional Court, the Supreme Court, and any High Court, from validating an act of high treason.

citations.act_or_case: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
citations.quote: An act of high treason mentioned in clause (1) or clause (2) shall not be validated by any court including the Federal Constitutional Court, Supreme Court and a High Court.

answer.short_answer: Nahi, Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 ki Section 39 ke mutabiq, court decree-holder ki darkhwast (application) par hi decree ko execution ke liye dusri court ko transfer kar sakti hai.
answer.explanation: Section 39(1) wazeh taur par bayan karti hai ke jis court ne decree pass ki hai, woh decree-holder ki application par hi usay execution ke liye kisi dusri court ko bhej sakti hai.

citations.quote: The Court which passed a decree may, on the application of the decree-holder, send it for execution to another Court

answer.short_answer: No, a public officer cannot be arrested or have their property attached during a lawsuit regarding their official duties, except in the execution of a decree.
answer.explanation: Under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, a public officer is exempt from arrest and the attachment of their property in suits concerning acts done in their official capacity, unless it is to execute a decree.

citations.quote: In a suit instituted against a public officer in respect of any act purporting to be done by him in his official capacity__ (a) the defendant shall not be liable to arrest nor his property to attachment otherwise than in execution of a decree

answer.short_answer: جی ہاں، کوڈ آف سول پروسیجر 1908 کی سیکشن 86A کے تحت سفارتی نمائندے کے خلاف قانونی کارروائی اس صورت میں کی جا سکتی ہے جب معاملہ اس کی نجی حیثیت میں پاکستان میں موجود کسی نجی غیر منقولہ جائیداد سے متعلق ہو۔
answer.explanation: قانون کے مطابق کسی سفارتی نمائندے کے خلاف عدالت میں کوئی کارروائی نہیں کی جا سکتی، سوائے اس کے کہ معاملہ اس کی نجی ملکیت میں موجود غیر منقولہ جائیداد سے متعلق ہو۔

citations.quote: No proceeding in any Court shall lie against a diplomatic agent except in a case relating to__ (a) any private immoveable property situated in Pakistan held by him in his private capacity

answer.short_answer: Yes, a High Court may order the execution of a decree before the costs of the suit have been ascertained by taxation.
answer.explanation: If a High Court deems it necessary, it may order the execution of a decree passed in its original civil jurisdiction before costs are calculated, provided that the execution excludes the portion relating to costs until those costs are ascertained.

citations.quote: the Court may order that the decree shall be executed forthwith, except as to so much thereof as relates to the costs; and, as to so much thereof as relates to the costs, that the decree may be executed as soon as the amount of the costs shall be ascertained by taxation.

answer.short_answer: No, two individuals cannot be considered associates solely because they are both employees of the same company.
answer.explanation: The Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 explicitly states that the status of associates does not arise merely because two persons are employees of the same third person.

citations.quote: Two persons shall not be associates solely by reason of the fact that one person is an employee of the other or both persons are employees of a third person.

answer.short_answer: No, mutual funds and insurance companies are subject to specific treatment regarding capital gain computation under Section 100B.
answer.explanation: While Section 100B(1) excludes mutual funds and insurance companies from the general rules of the Eighth Schedule, Section 100B(3) mandates that the NCCPL must compute and determine their capital gains according to the mechanism in Section 37A, while they continue to deposit tax as per the Ordinance's applicable provisions.

citations.quote: The provisions of sub–section (1) shall not apply to the following persons or class of persons, namely:- (a) a mutual fund; banking company [ ] and an insurance company subject to tax under the Fourth Schedule

NCCPL, in case of banking company, insurance company and mutual funds, shall compute and determine the capital gain as per the mechanism prescribed under section 37A; however, these entities shall continue to deposit tax on the amount of capital gain as per the applicable provisions of this Ordinance.

answer.short_answer: جی ہاں، اگر آپ کو کسی شخص پر دہشت گردی کا شک ہو تو آپ پولیس افسر کو اس بارے میں مطلع کر سکتے ہیں۔
answer.explanation: انسداد دہشت گردی ایکٹ کے تحت، کوئی بھی شخص پولیس افسر پر اپنا شک یا یقین ظاہر کر سکتا ہے کہ کوئی شخص دہشت گردی سے حاصل ہونے والی جائیداد رکھتا ہے یا دہشت گردی میں ملوث ہے۔

citations.quote: کوئی شخص پولیس افسر پر: (الف) یہ شک یا یقین ظاہر کر سکتا ہے کہ کوئی شخص رقم یا دگر جائیداد دہشت گردی جائیداد یا ملکیت ہے یا دہشت گردی سے ملنے والی جائیداد سے حاصل کردہ ہے ؛ یا (ب) ایسا مواد یا جو شک پر مبنی ہو

answer.short_answer: A person sentenced by an Anti-terrorism Court must file an appeal to the High Court within fifteen days of the passing of the sentence.
answer.explanation: According to the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, an appeal against a final judgment by an Anti-terrorism Court can be preferred by the sentenced person to the High Court within a period of fifteen days from the date the sentence is passed.

citations.quote: An appeal under sub-section (1) may be preferred by a person sentenced by 1[an Anti- terrorismCourt] to 1[a High Court] within 2[fifteen] days of the passing of the sentence.

answer.short_answer: If a wife exercises her delegated right to divorce (Talaq-e-Tafweez) or if parties seek to dissolve a marriage through means other than talaq, the provisions of Section 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961, apply mutatis mutandis.
answer.explanation: The law mandates that the procedural framework established for talaq, which includes providing written notice to the Chairman and the constitution of an Arbitration Council for reconciliation, must be followed with necessary modifications for these other forms of marriage dissolution.

citations.quote: Where the right to divorce has been. duly delegated to the wife and she wishes to exercise that right, or where any of the parties to a marriage wishes to dissolve the marriage otherwise than by talaq, the provisions of section 7 shall, mutatis mutandis and so far as applicable, apply.

The same procedural framework, with necessary modifications, also applies to the dissolution of marriage otherwise than by talaq, including cases where the husband has delegated the right of divorce to the wife.

answer.short_answer: Agar Union Council ka Chairman non-Muslim ho, toh Council apne Muslim members mein se kisi ek ko Chairman muntakhib (elect) karegi.
answer.explanation: Muslim Family Laws Ordinance ke mutabiq, agar Union Council ka Chairman non-Muslim ho, toh Arbitration Council ke maqasid ke liye Council ke Muslim members mein se kisi ek ko Chairman chuna jayega.

citations.quote: Provided that where the Chairman of the Union Council is a non- Muslim, or he himself wishes to make an application to the Arbitration Council, or is, owing to illness or any other reason, unable to discharge the functions of Chairman, the Council shall elect one of its Muslim members as Chairman for the purposes of this Ordinance

answer.short_answer: Where immediate action is required, an investigating officer may conduct a search and seizure with the prior permission of a senior officer of the concerned agency who is not below the rank of BS-20.
answer.explanation: Under the Anti-Money Laundering Act, 2010, while search and seizure powers generally require prior court permission, a proviso allows for immediate action to be taken with the authorization of a senior officer of at least BS-20 rank.

citations.quote: Provided that where immediate action is required, the powers of search and seizure shall be exercisable with prior permission of senior officer of the concerned investigating or prosecuting agency not below the rank of an officer of BS-20.

answer.short_answer: Ji haan, BS-17 aur us se upar ke civil servants ki assets ki tafseelat public ke liye available hoti hain.
answer.explanation: Civil Servants Act, 1973 ke mutabiq, BS-17 aur us se upar ke civil servants, unke spouse, aur dependent children ki assets ki declaration Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) ke paas digitally file ki jati hai aur yeh FBR ke zariye public ke liye available hoti hai.

citations.quote: the declaration of assets of a Civil Servant of BS-17 and above, his spouse and dependent children, including domestic and foreign assets and liabilities, as may be prescribed, shall be digitally filed with the Federal Board of Revenue and same shall be publicly available, through Federal Board of Revenue, in accordance with the rules as may be prescribed

answer.short_answer: Federal Board of Revenue Act, 2007, Section 19 ke tehat, Board tax-payers ko behtar sahuliyat faraham karne ke akhrajat, direct cost reimbursement, aur investment ya profit par munasib return ke liye fees ya charges laga sakta hai.
answer.explanation: Section 19 ke mutabiq, Board ko yeh ikhtiyar hasil hai ke woh tax-payers ke liye enhanced facilities, kharchon ki wapsi (reimbursement), aur public-private partnership ke tehat fiscal laws se mutaliq services faraham karne par fees ya charges lagaye.

citations.quote: The Board may levy any fee or charges for. making expenditure on the provision of enhanced facilities for the taxpayers, or direct cost reimbursement of expenses, and reasonable return on investment or profit; where services are provided in the matters relating to or under any fiscal law under public-private partnership.

answer.short_answer: Under the National Command Authority Act, 2010, the Appellate Authority is required to pass appropriate orders within ninety days of receiving an employee's appeal regarding their terms and conditions of service.
answer.explanation: The Act specifies that an employee aggrieved by an order, action, or inaction concerning their terms and conditions of service may appeal to the prescribed Appellate Authority, which must then provide a personal hearing and issue a decision within the ninety-day timeframe.

citations.quote: The Appellate Authority may provide personal hearing to the applicant and pass appropriate orders within ninety days of the receipt of application.

answer.short_answer: The Provincial Government argued that the 2001 Ordinance fundamentally changed the legal position by redefining "licensee" to include entities using generators over 500 KW for self-use, thereby withdrawing the exemption previously granted by the 1985 notification.
answer.explanation: The Provincial Government contended that while private entities using generators over 500 KW for self-use may have been exempt under the 1985 notification, the 2001 Ordinance's new definition of "licensee" statutorily classified them as such, effectively nullifying their prior protection.

citations.quote: The case of the appellant Provincial Government, in a nutshell, is that up to 2001 the respondents may have been entitled to the benefit of the 1985 notification but thereafter the position changed fundamentally on account of the new definition of “licensee” substituted by the 2001 Ordinance. In terms of the last portion thereof (“any person generating the electric power from a generator having the capacity of more than five hundred kilowatt for self use”) they statutorily became licensees. Any protection that they may have had in terms of the 1985 notification stood withdrawn by the 2001 notification

answer.short_answer: Supreme Court ne Tribunal ke us faislay ko illegal qarar diya jis mein 2015 se hone wali tamam promotions ko revert karne ka hukam diya gaya tha.
answer.explanation: Supreme Court ne note kiya ke Tribunal ne apne ikhtiyarat se tajawuz karte hue aur mutasireen ko sune baghair (right of audience) 2015 se hone wali tamam promotions ko revert karne ka hukam diya, jo ke fair trial aur due process ki khilaf warzi thi.

citations.quote: The directions of reverting all employees promoted since 2015 without making them party or without issuing any notice to them for providing the right of audience was illegal which seriously affected countless individuals.

answer.short_answer: Police authorities are legally obligated to immediately execute the arrest of an accused person once a court has dismissed their pre-arrest bail application.
answer.explanation: Investigating officers must act upon court orders dismissing pre-arrest bail without delay, regardless of whether a petition has been filed in a higher forum, unless an express stay order has been granted by a competent court.

citations.quote: This Court, therefore, finds it imperative to state clearly that investigating officers and police authorities are legally bound to act upon court orders dismissing pre-arrest bail immediately, without waiting for further instructions or presuming the existence of any stay where none has been granted.
Absent such an order, a refusal of bail remains fully operative and must be implemented promptly and in good faith by investigating authorities.

answer.short_answer: Before ordering substituted service, the Court must be satisfied that the defendant is avoiding service or that the summons cannot be served in the ordinary way.
answer.explanation: The Court is required to satisfy itself that the defendant is intentionally keeping out of the way to avoid service or that ordinary service is not possible. Additionally, the Court must adhere to the mandatory procedure prescribed by law to ensure the defendant is not condemned unheard.

citations.quote: Where the Court is satisfied that there is reason to believe that. the defendant is keeping out of the way for the purpose of avoiding service, or that for any other reason the summons cannot be served in the ordinary way, the Court shall order for service of summons

citations.act_or_case: Hashim Khan and others v. Mst. Musarat Begum and others (2025 SCMR 564)
citations.quote: the Court, before resorting to substituted service under Order V, Rule 20, C.P.C., must satisfy itself that ordinary service could not be effected and must adhere to the mandatory procedure prescribed by law.

answer.short_answer: The Supreme Court held that a cheque payment alone is not conclusive proof of a valid sale transaction in the absence of an agreement to sell or other corroborative evidence.
answer.explanation: The Court determined that producing a cheque payment without establishing the underlying transaction fails to meet the legal standard required to validate the alienation of immovable property, especially when the transfer is made by an attorney to their own sons without the principal's consent.

citations.quote: The alleged payment through cheque, made by the appellant (brother) in favour of the respondent (sister), is not conclusive proof of a valid sale transaction, particularly in the absence of any agreement to sell or other independent corroborative evidence reflecting a lawful bargain. Mere production of such payment, without establishing the underlying transaction, does not satisfy the legal standard required to validate an alienation of immovable property.

answer.short_answer: Under the 2001 Ordinance, a failure to collect advance tax triggers Section 161, which deems the person a taxpayer in default and activates Section 163.
answer.explanation: When a person required to collect advance tax fails to do so, they are considered a taxpayer in default under Section 161. This triggers Section 163, which mandates that the amount required to be collected is treated as tax due under an assessment order.

citations.quote: This alleged failure, according to the Department, triggered s. 161 of the 2001 Ordinance which, inter alia, applies when a person who is required to deduct or collect advance tax fails to do so. Such failure makes that person a deemed taxpayer in default
The provisions of this Ordinance shall apply to any amount required to be paid to the Commissioner under this Division as if it were tax due under an assessment order

answer.short_answer: The Supreme Court of Pakistan ruled that the forfeiture of the performance guarantee by the Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) was justified and set aside the lower courts' orders directing its refund.
answer.explanation: The Supreme Court allowed TCP's appeal, determining that the forfeiture of the performance guarantee was justified and reasonable under the circumstances, thereby overturning the previous judgments of the Sindh High Court that had ordered the refund.

citations.quote: the performance guarantee by TCP was justified and reasonable in the facts and circumstances of the case. ... The judgments of the learned Single Judge and the Division Bench of the Sindh High Court, insofar as they direct refund of the performance guarantee, are hereby set aside.

answer.short_answer: Supreme Court ne yeh observation di hai ke agar petitioner (baap) apni beti ke khilaf maintenance ka suit wapas nahi leta, toh Court apne faislay par nazar-e-sani (review) karegi.
answer.explanation: Supreme Court ne note kiya ke petitioner ne apni beti ke khilaf maintenance ka suit is bunyad par file kiya tha ke woh kama rahi hai. Jab petitioner ke wakeel ne suit wapas lene ka bayan diya, toh Court ne wazeh kiya ke agar suit wapas na liya gaya toh woh apne faislay par dobara gaur karenge.

citations.quote: In the event the suit is not withdrawn by the petitioner, this fact would cause us to review our judgment.

answer.short_answer: The core controversy concerns the allocation of reserved seats for women and non-Muslims to political parties in the National and Provincial Assemblies in accordance with Articles 51(6)(d), 51(6)(e), and 106(3)(c) of the Constitution.
answer.explanation: The Supreme Court identified that the primary issue for determination is the proper allocation of these reserved seats to political parties, specifically addressing whether parties are entitled to these seats based on their numerical strength and the requirements for contesting elections or submitting candidate lists.

citations.quote: The core controversy requiring resolution relates to the allocation of reserved seats for women and non-Muslims to political parties in the National Assembly and Provincial Assemblies in accordance with Article 51(6)(d) and (e) and Article 106(3)(c) of the Constitution, respectively.

answer.short_answer: High Court of Sindh ne apni 7 November 2024 ki judgment mein wukala ki janib se apne clients ke khilaf FIRs darj karwane ke trend ko ek aisi ahem paish-raft qarar diya hai jis par fori tawajo ki zaroorat hai.
answer.explanation: Supreme Court ke record ke mutabiq, High Court of Sindh ne apni judgment mein wukala ki janib se clients ke khilaf darj karwayi gayi FIRs ki tafseelat bayan ki hain aur is trend ko ek ahem mamla qarar diya hai.

answer.short_answer: In FIR No. 379/2026, the accused Allah Yar filed an application before the learned Area Magistrate Section-30, Kabirwala, requesting the constitution of a medical board to examine specific Medico-Legal Certificates, which was dismissed on May 21, 2026.
answer.explanation: The procedural history indicates that the accused, Allah Yar, sought the formation of a medical board regarding Medico-Legal Examination Certificates numbered 104/2026 through 107/2026, but this request was denied by the Magistrate.

citations.quote: Allah Yar (mentioned above) filed application before learned Area Magistrate Section-30, Kabirwala for constituting medical board regarding Medico-Legal Examination Certificates bearing Nos. 104/2026, 105/2026, 106/2026 and 107/2026 of Muhammad Waseem, Faisal Nadeem, Muhammad Amir and Muhammad Nawaz (present petitioner) respectively, copy of the application is available at page Nos.15-16 of this petition as annexure-C, which was dismissed vide order dated: 21.05.2026 passed by learned Magistrate Section-30, Kabirwala

answer.short_answer: The appellate court awarded Rs. 3,500 per month to each of the four minor children and Rs. 4,000 per month to the wife.
answer.explanation: In the case referenced, the appellate court modified the trial court's decree, setting the maintenance for the four minor petitioners at Rs. 3,500 each with a 10% annual increment, and for the wife (petitioner No. 5) at Rs. 4,000 per month.

citations.quote: The learned appellate court vide judgment and decree dated 30.11.2018 modified the decree of the learned trial court and held the minor petitioners No. 1 to 4 entitled to receive maintenance W.P.No.10200 of 2019 allowance @ Rs. 3500/- each from the date of institution of the suit till their legal entitlement with 10% annual increment, whereas the petitioner No. 5 was held entitled to receive Rs. 4000/- per month as maintenance from the institution of the suit till subsistence of marriage or in case of divorce till “iddat” period.

answer.short_answer: Yes, a person who provides necessaries to an individual incapable of contracting is entitled to be reimbursed from that individual's property.
answer.explanation: Under the Contract Act, 1872, if a person who is incapable of entering into a contract, or anyone they are legally bound to support, is supplied with necessaries suited to their condition in life, the supplier has a legal right to be reimbursed from the property of the incapable person.

citations.quote: If a person, incapable of entering into a contract, or any one whom he is legally bound to support, is supplied by another person with necessaries suited to his condition in life, the person who has furnished such supplies is entitled to be reimbursed from the property of such incapable person.

answer.short_answer: The Lahore High Court set aside the judgment and decree dated 16.02.2019 passed by the Additional District Judge, Gujrat, and restored the trial court's judgment, thereby decreeing the petitioners' suit for declaration, cancellation of mutations, and permanent injunction.
answer.explanation: In Civil Revision No.27111 of 2019, the Lahore High Court found that the Appellate Court failed to properly address material aspects of the case, warranting interference. Consequently, it set aside the Appellate Court's decision and restored the original decree of the Civil Judge, Gujrat.

citations.quote: Consequently, the instant civil revision is allowed. The impugned judgment and decree dated 16.02.2019 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Gujrat, are hereby set aside, and the consolidated judgment and decree dated 07.03.2016 passed by the learned Civil Judge, Gujrat, are restored. Resultantly, the petitioners' suit for declaration, cancellation of the disputed mutations and permanent injunction stands decreed in terms of the judgment of the learned Trial Court

answer.short_answer: The Lahore High Court set aside the impugned order dated 06.10.2026 regarding the maintainability of the complaint and remanded the matter to the Consumer Court for a fresh decision.
answer.explanation: The High Court determined that the Consumer Court's previous finding on maintainability was flawed and directed it to re-examine the issue in accordance with the law and relevant statutory provisions, specifically Sections 122(1)(a) and 122(3) of the Ordinance.

citations.quote: The impugned order dated 06.10.2026, passed by the Presiding Officer, District Consumer Court, Bhakkar, is set aside only to the extent of the determination of the question of maintainability of the complaint instituted by the Respondent No.1. The matter is remanded to the Consumer Court with the direction to decide the question of maintainability afresh, strictly in accordance with law

answer.short_answer: Lahore High Court ne F.I.R. No. 1157 of 2016 ke appellants ko bari kar diya hai.
answer.explanation: Lahore High Court ne apne faislay mein Imran Javed, Khan Tehseen Arshi, aur Haider Ali ko bari karne ka hukum diya aur unhein fori tor par jail se riha karne ki hidayat ki, agar woh kisi aur case mein matloob na hon.

citations.quote: The appellants, Imran Javed, son of Javed Iqbal Khan, Khan Tehseen Arshi, son of Nazir Hussain Chishti and Haider Ali, son of Khan Tehseen Arshi, are in jail and are directed to be released forthwith if not required in any other case.
